definitions.explanation: Describes something so common that it is unremarkable or uninteresting. Often carries a slightly dismissive or negative nuance, implying a lack of originality or distinction.

examples.japanese: ありふれた{話|はなし}だ。
ありふれた{日常|にちじょう}の{中|なか}にも{幸|しあわ}せはある。
examples.english: There is happiness even in ordinary daily life.

examples.japanese: ありふれた{名前|なまえ}だが、{彼|かれ}はとても{個性的|こせいてき}な{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He has a common name, but he is a very unique person.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
This is the past-tense form of the verb {有|あ}り{触|ふ}れる (to be commonly found), but it functions as a prenominal adjective modifying nouns directly. The base verb form ありふれる is rarely used on its own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ありふれた{話|はなし} (a commonplace story)
- ありふれた{日常|にちじょう} (ordinary daily life)
- ありふれた{光景|こうけい} (a common sight)
- ありふれた{名前|なまえ} (a common name)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {平凡|へいぼん}: ordinary, mediocre (na-adjective, more neutral)
- {普通|ふつう}: normal, ordinary (more neutral, no negative nuance)
